subject: Two layer in one figure, plus facet?

messages.author: 56f89e4e966f65cf
messages.subject: Two layer in one figure, plus facet?
parts:
Dears,

Here's my question:

I have a dataset A, with a column 'year'; now I can draw a graph like this:  

ggplot(A,...)+facet_wrap(~year)

I also have another dataset B, also contain a 'year' column. I can also draw like:

ggplot(B,...)+geom_vline(...)+facet_wrap(~year)

Now, How can I put these two layers in one graph? (with facet)


Thanks a lot lot!

ZJ

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Two layer in one figure, plus facet?
parts:
Sounds to me like you could do that by creating a new variable (A and B) and appending the two datasets together with rbind() or merge() or plyr::rbind.fill() then plotting them together. 

#shows different data by different color can also use shape?
ggplot(AB, aes(colour=AB),...) + geom_vline(...) + facet_wrap(~year)

parts:
require(plyr)
require(ggplot2)

#create some data
datA<- data.frame(Year=rep(2008, 10), value=rnorm(10, 55, 15), Time=1:10)
datB<- data.frame(Year=rep(2008, 5), value=rnorm(5, 55, 15), Time=1:5)

#append new variable
datA$AB<-"A"
datB$AB<-"B"

#bind the 2 datasets together
datC<-rbind.fill(datA, datB)

#plot them, not the best example, but you get the idea...
ggplot(datC, aes(x=Time, y=value, colour=AB, group=AB))+geom_line()
